2607.18045.title: The Shared Discovery Paradox: How a One-Answer Rule Turns Better Information into Worse Search
2607.18045.paper_summary: Organizations often pool dispersed information into one ranking and then allow many agents to act on that shared view. In a discovery problem, this can improve beliefs while reducing coverage. We develop an exactly solvable benchmark with sixteen boxes, one target, eight searchers, and noisy private clues. Pooling raises the accuracy of the best single recommendation from 0.20 to 0.3835, but repeating that recommendation lowers group discovery from 0.8322 under decentralized clue-following to 0.3835. A coordinated eight-action portfolio using the same pooled reports reaches 0.8594, and seven coordinated actions recover the decentralized benchmark. The paradox is a protocol failure, not an information failure: a one-answer rule compresses a portfolio of available actions into one repeated choice. We then replace the planner with self-interested searchers who split a prize. The equal-split game is a potential game. Its anonymous symmetric equilibrium obeys a water-filling rule. In the canonical instance it achieves 0.5991: strictly above consensus, but below both private search and the planner. The exact mixed price of anarchy is 2 - 1/N. A sole-rescue reward, which pays only an agent who covers the target alone, makes every pure Nash equilibrium first-best. Finally, a latent common-cue model shows how correlated reports collapse effective discovery channels. The centralized planner gain rises strictly with copying, and in the canonical environment the symmetric market overtakes decentralized report-following at copying probability c = 0.788462. In a proportional large-market limit the five-protocol ordering survives exactly: consensus discovery vanishes while blind, market, private, and portfolio search converge to 0.500, 0.547, 0.847, and 0.874. The contribution is a compact benchmark that separates information, allocation, incentives, and dependence into exact, reusable quantities.
2607.18045.paper_summary_zh: 組織經常將分散的信息整合成一個排名，然後允許許多代理根據這個共享的觀點行動。在發現問題中，這可以改善信念，同時減少覆蓋率。我們開發了一個精確可解的基準，包含十六個盒子、一個目標、八個搜尋者和嘈雜的私人線索。整合提高了最佳單一建議的準確性，從0.20提升到0.3835，但重複該建議使得群體發現從0.8322下降到0.3835，這是在去中心化的線索跟隨下的結果。使用相同整合報告的協調八行動組合達到0.8594，而七個協調行動則恢復了去中心化的基準。這一悖論是協議失敗，而非信息失敗：一個單一答案規則將可用行動的組合壓縮為一個重複的選擇。我們隨後用自利的搜尋者取代計劃者，他們分配獎勵。平分獎勵的遊戲是一個潛在遊戲。它的匿名對稱均衡遵循水填充規則。在典型情況下，它達到0.5991：嚴格高於共識，但低於私人搜尋和計劃者。混合無政府狀態的確切價格為2 - 1/N。單一救援獎勵僅支付覆蓋目標的代理，使每個純納什均衡達到最佳。最後，一個潛在的共同線索模型顯示了相關報告如何崩潰有效的發現渠道。集中計劃者的收益隨著複製的增加而嚴格上升，在典型環境中，對稱市場在複製概率c = 0.788462下超越去中心化報告跟隨。在一個比例大型市場的極限中，五個協議的排序恰好存活：共識發現消失，而盲目、市場、私人和組合搜尋收斂到0.500、0.547、0.847和0.874。這項貢獻是一個緊湊的基準，將信息、分配、激勵和依賴分離為精確的、可重用的量。
2607.18045.author: Yohei Nakajima et.al.
